clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old female initially presented with nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. A thorough GI workup, including MRCP, was negative. Subsequently, she developed progressively worsening bilateral eye redness and signs of renal dysfunction, including proteinuria (900 mg/dL) and elevated serum creatinine (2.5). A kidney biopsy was performed, revealing marked interstitial infiltrate with tubulitis and focal tubular epithelial cell necrosis, consistent with Acute Interstitial Nephritis (AIN). An ophthalmologic examination confirmed bilateral anterior uveitis with keratic precipitates and posterior synechiae. With the diagnosis of anterior uveitis and AIN, TINU syndrome was confirmed.
